static.description: A Spring Boot travel assistance application providing a REST API for managing trips (CRUD operations) with JPA persistence, built with Kotlin and Spring Modulith.
domain_concepts: Trip: The core domain entity representing a travel trip with title, description, destination, and date range, persisted in the 'trips' table.
TripDto: A data transfer object used for creating and updating Trip entities, with validation constraints (e.g., title must not be blank).
TripRepository: Spring Data JPA repository interface providing standard CRUD operations for the Trip entity.
TripService: Service layer encapsulating business logic for trip CRUD operations with transactional support.
TripController: REST controller exposing trip management endpoints under /api/trips with standard HTTP methods.

dynamic.architecture_summary: A standard Spring Boot layered architecture (Controller → Service → Repository) using Spring Data JPA for persistence against an H2 in-memory database. The project uses Spring Modulith for modular design and Netflix DGS codegen for GraphQL client generation. Kotlin data classes serve as both JPA entities and DTOs with Jakarta validation.

agent_safe_operations: Add new endpoints to TripController following the existing REST pattern
Add new fields to Trip entity and TripDto (with corresponding service/controller updates)
Add new service classes following the existing @Service pattern
Add new repository interfaces extending JpaRepository
Add new test classes in the test directory
Modify application.properties or application.yml for configuration changes
Add new DTOs in the dto package
Add new model entities in the model package
agent_forbidden_operations: Modify or delete Gradle wrapper files (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/*)
Change the Spring Boot or Kotlin version in build.gradle.kts without explicit instruction
Remove or rename the main application class TravelAssistApplication
Switch the database from H2 to a production database without explicit instruction
Modify settings.gradle.kts project name without understanding downstream impacts
Add secrets or credentials directly in source code or configuration files
potential_pitfalls: The project uses Spring Boot 4.0.4 which is a very recent/cutting-edge version — some plugins or libraries may have compatibility issues
Kotlin data classes used as JPA entities require special care: the Trip entity uses var for mutable fields but val for id, which is correct but fragile if changed
The DGS codegen plugin expects GraphQL schemas in src/main/resources/graphql-client but this directory may not exist yet — builds may fail on the generateJava task
H2 is the only configured database (runtime dependency) — there are no production database configurations
compose.yaml exists suggesting Docker Compose integration via spring-boot-docker-compose, but the file contents are unknown
The @Xannotation-default-target=param-property compiler flag affects how annotations are applied to Kotlin data class properties — removing it could break validation
Lombok is included as a dependency but is largely unnecessary in a Kotlin project — it may cause confusion
Both application.properties and application.yml exist — Spring Boot loads both, and conflicting keys may cause unexpected behavior
